body.statement: For every finite sample, \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}\) is positive definite, all block inverses in def:multiplier-ellipses exist, and the conditional critical value \(\widehat c_{1-\gamma}\) is well defined in \([0,\infty)\). Conditionally on the data, \(Z^\star\) consistently estimates the law of \(\sqrt{n/L_n}(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))\), and the ridged ellipses obey \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\{\tau_j(P)\in\mathcal E_j\text{ for all }1\leq j\leq J\}\to1-\gamma\).
body.justification: The multiplier law has the right conditional Gaussian form and a continuous parameter-free limit only if both parent convergence results hold.
body.gap: The joint limit and covariance consistency are both still open.
body.consumer: The displayed ellipses are a proposed procedure without a current coverage theorem.

obligation.what_is_open: Transfer an established joint critical limit and consistent covariance estimate through the conditional multiplier maximum law.
obligation.obstruction: Both probabilistic parent results remain open after the harmonic audit, so coverage cannot presently be asserted even though the ridge totalizes every finite sample.
obligation.attempted: The conditional Gaussian law of the multiplier and the parameter-free continuous limiting maximum of independent blockwise chi-square variables were derived.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditionally on the data, the Gaussian multipliers give the exact identity
\[
 Z^\star\mid\text{data}\sim N(0,\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}).
\tag{14}
\]
If the joint critical limit and covariance consistency were established, the ridge \(\theta_n I_{2J}\) would vanish in operator norm, and (14) would converge conditionally to \(N(0,V(P))\).  Because \(V(P)\) is block diagonal and every \(V_j(P)\) is positive definite, the limiting statistic is
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}Z_j^{\mathsf T}V_j(P)^{-1}Z_j
 \ \stackrel{d}{=}\ \max_{1\leq j\leq J}Q_j,
 \qquad Q_1,\ldots,Q_J\ \text{independent }\chi_2^2.
\tag{15}
\]
Its distribution is continuous and parameter free, so conditional quantile convergence plus the joint central limit theorem would yield simultaneous coverage \(1-\gamma\).  The ridge already guarantees finite-sample invertibility.  Coverage remains open because neither parent convergence is presently established.
